items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: The interviewee (Dorothy Tait) does not speak about her own interactions with Papa John; the interviewer narrates an anecdote about Papa John interacting with Japanese musicians, and the interviewee only comments on the band's schedule.

ctx.x: Did you hear them in the Osaka? What was it?

Then, then there were several concerts in Tokyo. Then went to Osaka, to the Shin-Ozaka Hotel, where the band stayed and I stayed too. And there was a music hall around the corner. Again, absolutely huge, very plush. And now a fantastically enthusiastic response because Osaka was the center of the Japanese, the Dixieland Rascals, the Japanese band. And it was a fantastic And it was just mobbed. And terribly successful. And in the lobby of the hotel, there was a great chance for the Japanese to get to know the…

I believe they played in a soccer, but I think Jaffee said they played for something like 40 nights in a row. Yep. Is that right? He said that they were actually, that the festival hall where it was there, and they were actually packed out more every night.
